question.text: This company, based in Amsterdam, was given a monopoly on Dutch spice trade in 1602 and was one of the first major international corporations.
question.answerHtml: Dutch East India Company [accept United East Indian Company]
question.clue: Members of this group waterboarded and executed English merchants in the Amboyna massacre.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of the Netherlands, whose name literally means "low-lying countries"
swap.text: Part of the modern-day Netherlands gained independence from the Spanish Empire in a war named for this many years, which is how long it lasted.

question.text: The Dutch revolt against Spanish rule is generally known as this war, referring to its length. It was ended by the Peace of Munster and the independence of the Dutch Republic.
question.clue: Italian engineer Frederico Giambelli helped design fire ships during this war, during which Balthasar Gerard assassinated a leader.

swap.text: During his reign, Mobutu renamed his capital city to Kinshasa. Previously, Kinshasa was named for this Belgian king who committed atrocities while he owned the Congo Free State.
swap.answerHtml: Leopold II of Belgium (prompt on Leopold or Leopoldville alone) (Kinshasa’s original name was Leopoldville)
swap.clue: E. D. Morel co-founded a group aimed at reforming a territory controlled by this ruler along with Roger Casement, whose namesake report detailed atrocities in that territory.

question.leadin: The Manifesto of the 93 was signed in defense of actions committed by German soldiers in this country.
question.text: Name this country invaded on August 4, 1914, in accord with the Schlieffen Plan, despite having declared itself to be neutral.
question.answerHtml: Belgium [or Kingdom of Belgium or Royaume de Belgique or Koninkrijk Belgie or Königreich Belgien]
question.clue: World War I fighting in this country included the first use of chlorine gas during the Battle of Ypres .

swap.leadin: This country had a colony at Tianjin in China.
swap.text: Name this country whose capital is Brussels. This country's other colonial ventures included a stint in Guatemala and as co-ruler of the Moroccan Tangier International Zone.
swap.answerHtml: Kingdom of Belgium [accept Koninkrijk België, accept Royaume de Belgique, accept Königreich Belgien]
swap.clue: One of this country's rulers was criticized in the Casement Report, and that same ruler created an army called the Force Publique.

question.leadin: A rejected 1937 law in this country was derisively nicknamed the Maulkuerfgesetz, or the "muzzle law," and sought to outlaw the Communist Party.
question.text: Name this "Gibraltar of the North" which helps to name a European zone with Belgium and the Netherlands.
question.clue: Known as the Gibraltar of the North, this nation's fortifications were improved upon by Vauban under Louis XIV.

swap.leadin: In September of 1944, over 40,000 allied paratroopers were dropped near Arnhem in the Netherlands in an ambitious plan to end World War 2 by Christmas.
swap.text: Name this failed operation. Its success depended on the taking and holding of several bridges.
swap.clue: It was the last attempt to win the war by Christmas and had a strategic objective of forcing a crossing of the at .

question.text: This Flemish city saw half of its population flee in 1585 when the brutal "Spanish Fury" looted its besieged buildings and killed thousands of residents.
question.clue: Echoing Rome, the people of this city affixed the letters SPQA to its pioneering Beurs building.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the violent history of Europe.
swap.text: Organized by the Duke of Alba, this court in the Spanish Netherlands attempted to suppress Calvinism and tighten Spanish control over the Netherlands by enforcing the Tenth Penny tax.
swap.answerHtml: Council of Blood [or Council of Troubles; or Raad Van Beroerten; or Bloedraad; or Tribunal de los Revoltosos; or Tribunal de Sangre; accept reasonable equivalents for "Council", such as "Court" ]
swap.clue: This tribunal created by the Duke of Alba to deal with unrest in the early stages of the Dutch Revolt.

question.leadin: The death of this ideology was blamed on an increased trade union syndicalism, the threat of Irish Civil War, and Conservative opposition to the Parliament Act in one work.
question.text: The strange death of this ideology was written about in a book by George Dangerfield, which he claims took place between 1910 and 1914. Henry Campbell-Bannerman was a Prime Minister who led a party named for this ideology.
question.clue: This word describes a series of reforms carried out in Britain after the election of Henry Campbell-Bannerman that were financed by the People's Budget.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the potato in European history.
swap.text: The 1917 "Potato Riots" took place in this country due to the export of potatoes to Britain and Germany for coal. The Germans built an electric fence called the "Wire of Death" along this country's southern border during the war.
swap.clue: This country withdrew from Formosa after being defeated by Koxinga, and it introduced technology known as rangaku through its control of Dejima.

question.text: This University of Leuven scholar, who created a 1569 world map, led the "golden age of Netherlandish cartography." This engraver, who coined the term "atlas," names a widely-used but controversial map "projection."
question.clue: This Belgian-born cartographer is known today for his namesake style of projection, which distorts the poles.

swap.leadin: Yab Yum was closed when this city's court successfully argued its owner Hennie Vittali conducted illegal business there as a frontman for Hells Angels.
swap.text: The Yab Yum brothel operated in the Singelgebied, which along with De Wallen and Ruysdaelkade comprises the Rosse Buurt of this Dutch city on the Amstel river.
swap.clue: Princess Beatrix's 1966 marriage to a German noble was protested in this city due to his previous membership in Hitler Youth.

question.text: During the Red River Rebellion, Riel's government executed Thomas Scott, a member of an order of this name. A ruler from a European dynasty with this name was assassinated by Balthasar Gerard.
question.clue: Previous members had been princes of its namesake city as well as staathalters.

swap.leadin: Hubert Pierlot declared a king of this name unfit to govern and appointed his brother Prince Charles as regent after he refused to join Pierlot's government in exile.
swap.text: Give this name of a king who abdicated in 1950 because of a general strike over his 1940 surrender to the Nazis. Adam Hochschild detailed the atrocities of that man's uncle of the same name in a book on his "ghost."
swap.clue: Atrocities committed under a king of this name were detailed in the Casement Report which included accounts of his Force Publique severing the limbs of workers who failed to meet rubber quotas.

question.leadin: Near the end of the Eighty Years' War a Spanish fleet carrying troops to Flanders was overtaken by a Dutch fleet of only eighteen ships, which forced the Spanish to withdraw to the neutral waters of England; a month later, the rest of the Dutch broke neutrality and destroyed the Spanish.
question.text: Name this battle of October 21, 1639, which broke the naval power of Spain and made the reputation of the winning admiral.

swap.leadin: Galbert of Bruges wrote a history called On The Murder, Betrayal, and Slaughter of [this man], The Glorious One.
swap.text: Name this beatified count of Flanders who was killed in the church of Saint Donatian by agents of the Erembalds, a powerful family that he tried to demote to serfdom. He was succeeded by William Clito, the grandson of William the Conqueror.
swap.answerHtml: Charles the Good [or Charles the Good, Count of Flanders; or Charles I, Count of Flanders]

question.leadin: Answer the following about the military career of some guy named Eugene. FTPE.
question.text: In this 1708 battle, roughly a year before Malplaquet, Eugene crushed the Duke of Vendome outside a town in southern Belgium, driving the duke out of the war for an extended period.

swap.leadin: Since their pay had been confiscated by Elizabeth I en route to them, angry Spanish tercios decided to carry out this action as a way of compensating themselves for their lost wages.
swap.text: Name this 1576 action, sometimes called the Spanish Fury, in which forces under Sancho d'Avila pillaged a wealthy port city for three days straight. Rather than breaking the will of the revolting Dutch, this event instead strengthened their resolve.
swap.clue: Otto Oberstein, drowned in the Scheldt while retreating from it, and the five thousand troops under the Marquis de Havre mostly failed to offer any resistance.
